channel.title: Bike Stories Blog
channel.description: Practical bike maintenance, what wears out when, and what a bike really costs — from the team behind Bike Stories.

item.title: Kids' bikes: five things worth paying for
item.description: Which features on a kids' bike are worth the money — weight, brakes, fit, tyres, gearing — how to check each in the shop, and the ones that don't matter.

item.title: Winter riding: what salt and grit destroy first on your bike
item.description: Winter riding is not that bad for you — it is for a short list of consumables. What salt and grit destroy first, and the habits that slow it down.

item.title: When to replace a cassette and chainring, and when they go as a set
item.description: How to tell when your cassette and chainring are actually worn, why a new chain can make the skipping worse, and when the whole drivetrain has to go as a set.

item.title: A child's first pedal bike: balance bike or stabilisers
item.description: Balance bike first, pedals second. What each route teaches, when a child is ready for pedals, and the brake and setup checks before the first ride off.

item.title: What size bike a kid actually needs — inseam and standover, not age
item.description: How to size a child's bike from inseam and standover instead of an age chart, plus the brake-reach check that decides whether they can stop it.

item.title: Bike wheel rattling: hub and bearing wear, checked in ten minutes
item.description: Loose or rough bearings are a wear part with a test, not a guess: the spin-down check, the hand-roller method for play, and what a service or replace costs.

item.title: Why that tyre is so hard to mount — and how to seat it properly
item.description: Why a tyre fights you at the final third, and the tools and technique that put it on straight — bead tension, lever order, and the rim tape check first.

item.title: Chain lube: wet, dry, wax, and which one your conditions actually want
item.description: Wet lube for wet roads, dry lube for grit and sun, hot wax for the people who actually do it — and the one chain fact that beats every lube in the shop.
